title: Anadolu Kavağı, Yoros Castle & Full Bosphorus Ferry Day Trip
seoTitle: Anadolu Kavağı & Yoros Castle: Bosphorus Ferry Day Trip
metaDescription: Plan the Şehir Hatları full Bosphorus ferry to Anadolu Kavağı: Yoros Castle hike, seafood lunch timing, return boat, and private options.
quickAnswer: The municipal Şehir Hatları Long Bosphorus Tour sails north from Eminönü past Ottoman waterfront mansions to the fishing village of Anadolu Kavağı, near the Black Sea mouth. Passengers receive roughly three hours ashore—enough time to hike up to Byzantine Yoros Castle, eat grilled seasonal fish by the pier, and catch the scheduled afternoon ferry back to central Istanbul.

body.text: How does the Şehir Hatları full-Bosphorus ferry to Anadolu Kavağı work?

The [Şehir Hatları Long Bosphorus Tour](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/bosphorus-tours/long-bosphorus-tour-91) departs Eminönü in the morning, stops at Beşiktaş, Kanlıca, Sarıyer, and Rumeli Kavağı, and docks at Anadolu Kavağı roughly 95 minutes later. Unlike private tourist boats, it is a classic municipal ferry with open upper decks, indoor saloons, and an onboard tea counter.

Tickets are sold separately from standard commuter Istanbulkart rides at the dedicated Boğaz Turu kiosk beside Eminönü Pier; check current round-trip rates on the [Şehir Hatları Bosphorus Tour tariff page](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/tr/ucret-tarifeleri/bogaz-turlari-78). Arriving 30 minutes before departure helps you claim an outer bench on the upper deck—sitting on the port (left) side heading north gives clear views of Dolmabahçe Palace, Ortaköy Mosque, Rumeli Fortress, and the European-shore mansions.

For travellers who prefer commuter timing over the single tour sailing, Şehir Hatları also operates the regular [Anadolu Kavağı–Üsküdar commuter line](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/tr/seferler/ic-hatlar/bogaz-hatlari/anadolukavagi-uskudar-172), though sailings are spaced out and require checking the seasonal timetable in advance.
How steep is the walk up to Byzantine Yoros Castle overlooking the Black Sea?

The walk from Anadolu Kavağı pier to Yoros Castle takes 20 to 25 minutes uphill along a paved road and stepped footpath gaining roughly 120 metres in elevation. It is manageable for anyone comfortable with brisk stairs, though summer heat and exposed stretches make sturdy footwear and water essential.

Originally built as a Byzantine customs and defensive fortress guarding the Black Sea entrance, Yoros Castle sits directly above the narrow northern mouth of the strait. Today you walk along the outer stone walls and towers rather than entering a ticketed museum interior. From the grassy ridge just below the twin-towered gate, you can see cargo ships lining up in the Black Sea, the suspension towers of the Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge, and the twin hills of Rumeli Kavağı across the water.
If someone in your group prefers to skip the climb, local taxis wait near the ferry square and can drive up to the terrace cafés just below the castle gate in five minutes.
How long do you have for seafood lunch before the return ferry?

On the standard [Uzun Boğaz Turu schedule](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/tr/seferler/bogaz-turlari/uzun-bogaz-turu-91), the boat waits at Anadolu Kavağı until 15:00, giving you roughly two hours and forty-five minutes ashore. Doing the castle climb immediately upon disembarking leaves a comfortable 90 minutes for a relaxed waterfront lunch before boarding.

Anadolu Kavağı's waterfront is lined with family-run seafood restaurants that call out to arriving passengers. Rather than rushing into the first doorway, walk two minutes along the quay to compare chalkboard menus and check whether prices are listed per portion or per kilogram. Classic orders include fried midye tava (battered mussels with tarator sauce), calamari, shepherd's salad, and whatever seasonal Bosphorus fish—such as hamsi, palamut, or lüfer—was landed that morning.

body.text: When is a private boat better than the public ferry?

A private motor yacht or classic wooden boat makes more sense than the public ferry if you are travelling with a group of four or more, want to set your own departure time, or hope to stop at smaller Bosphorus piers such as Bebek, Kandilli, or Poyrazköy without waiting for a fixed 15:00 return.

Private charters also suit visitors with tight schedules—such as business travellers on a free afternoon or families with young children and older relatives who prefer shaded seating and step-free boarding directly from a hotel pier. Because Bosphorus boat pricing varies sharply by vessel quality, fuel, and captain reputation, working with an independent advisor helps avoid inflated tourist-dock quotes.

faq.q: Does the Long Bosphorus Tour run year-round?
faq.a: Yes, Şehir Hatları operates the Long Bosphorus Tour in both summer and winter timetables, though daily frequency changes by season. Heavy fog or winter storms near the Black Sea can occasionally cause short-notice cancellations.

faq.q: Can you use an Istanbulkart on the Long Bosphorus Tour?
faq.a: No. The dedicated Long Bosphorus Tour requires a separate tour ticket purchased at the pier kiosk. Standard commuter ferries on the Anadolu Kavağı–Üsküdar route do accept Istanbulkart.

faq.q: Is there an entrance fee for Yoros Castle?
faq.a: No ticket is required to walk up to the exterior ramparts and panoramic terrace around Yoros Castle. Only food, tea, or taxi rides to the hilltop carry a cost.

faq.q: What happens if you miss the 15:00 return ferry from Anadolu Kavağı?
faq.a: You are not stranded. You can take a municipal İETT bus south through Beykoz toward Üsküdar or Kavacık, or take a taxi across the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge back to the European side, though afternoon road traffic can add considerable time.

faq.q: Which side of the ferry has the best views?
faq.a: Heading north, the left (European) side passes closer to Dolmabahçe, Çırağan, Ortaköy, and Rumeli Fortress. On the return southbound trip, sitting on the opposite side highlights Kanlıca, Anadolu Hisarı, Küçüksu, and Beylerbeyi Palace.
